instrument: derivation-accounting — coverage ledger, NOT an oracle
question: 1,652 derivation sites on the parse tree produced 438 extends edges. Which sites produced no edge, and why?

corpus.admission: git ls-files tracked only, <= 512 KiB, detectLanguageFromPath(abs, text) === 'xml' — copied from script/m14/ontology-coverage-gate.ts:201-213 so the populations are the same sample

constants.source: read off RealXmlAnalyzer at run time (TypeScript `private` is erased), not copied or scraped

edgeAccounting.note: sites > edges is EXPECTED and not a defect on its own: a `derivation` edge is emitted per candidate, and XSD permits repeated `base` values across one file that collapse to the same (from, to) pair. The load-bearing row is edgesWithNoSiteBehindThem, which would be an edge with no parse-tree fact under it.

resolutionByResolvableClass.question: is `extends` low both-ends resolution a defect, or a property of XSD bases being BUILT-IN types this document does not declare?
resolutionByResolvableClass.note: targetIsSymbol is measured against the names the FILE declares. A builtin base is declared by XSD Part 2, not by this file, so it is expected to read false here and the edge is still true.

sourceAuthenticity.question: is each extends edge's SOURCE a name the document DECLARES, or a schema element's tag name the analyzer fell back to?
sourceAuthenticity.mechanism: src/ast/real-xml-analyzer.ts:824 computes symbolName = declaredName ?? name, and lines 908-925 pass that as the ownerName for the element's own attributes. For base= on an XSD derivation element there is no name=, so the owner becomes the tag text. The convention is right for type= on a named element and wrong for base=, whose owner is the nearest ANCESTOR that declares a name.

callsSourceAuthenticity.question: the extends question asked of `calls`: is each calls edge's SOURCE a name the document DECLARES, or an XSLT vocabulary tag?
callsSourceAuthenticity.note: `calls` resolves at 100% at both ends on every draw, which says nothing about this: the analyzer mints a symbol for whatever name an edge needs. A variable IS a legitimate caller when a call sits in an inline variable body, so 'declared-caller' covers template, variable, param, function and with-param alike.

callsSiteLedger.question: the fix dropped 146 calls edges (548 -> 402). Every xsl:call-template carrying a name is counted on the parse tree and classified, so the drop is a COUNT and not a rationale.
callsSiteLedger.note: A site with no named caller is one calls must NOT publish: XSLT 1.0 §2.4 does not permit an instruction sequence at stylesheet top level, so there is no caller to name. The `covered` count is expected to EXCEED the published edge count, because edge identity is the triple (source, type, target) and several sites in one template calling the same callee collapse.

referencesSourceAuthenticity.question: the extends/calls question asked of `references`, which resolves at 49.1% here against CSS's 66.8%. A resolution rate is the wrong instrument: a minted source resolves perfectly, so the source is asked directly.
referencesSourceAuthenticity.note: 'declared-in-file' means the file writes that name on SOME element's name= attribute, any namespace — a wide superset, since a references source is often an ordinary application element. Over-approximating declarations biases AGAINST calling a real source fabricated. 'undeclared' is NOT asserted to be wrong: a references source may legitimately be an element the document only CONTAINS (the analyzer publishes inline elements as symbols), so this class is reported, not judged. 'vocabulary-tag' requires an element in the XSD or XSLT namespace with that local name to be PRESENT IN THIS FILE; deciding it from a list of local names is what the first version did, and it filed db2-templates.xml's ordinary `<template name=...>` element as an XSLT tag.
referencesSourceAuthenticity.residualNote: the roles carrying the 111 edges that still name a vocabulary tag. The re-base gives a reference the nearest NAMED declaration; a site with no named declaration in scope has none to name, and the fallback keeps the pre-existing value rather than refusing the edge. `xslt_named_template_reference` at stylesheet top level and `entity_reference` under a `match=`-dispatched template are that shape.

limitations: A coverage ledger, not a correctness oracle: it finds sites that produced no edge. It cannot decide whether an emitted edge is right.

Class H is an UPPER bound: `declaredHere` counts only XSD declaration elements, a deliberate under-approximation of the analyzer's seven-place `declaredNames`. Under-approximating declarations can only move a site OUT of A into H, so it inflates H and never inflates A.
A-prefixed binding that IS a builtin or IS imported, yet still unmatched, would land in H. That is a real shortfall and H is where to look for it.
